title: Set screen resolution with xrandr
summary: Use xrandr to change the resolution of a specific monitor output. This change is temporary and lasts only for the current session.
prerequisites: Know your output name (e.g., HDMI-1, VGA-1) and desired resolution.

steps.explain: List available outputs and resolutions to find the correct output name and mode.
steps.expect: A list of outputs (e.g., HDMI-1 connected) and supported resolutions.

steps.explain: Set the resolution for the specific output. Replace <OUTPUT_NAME> and <RESOLUTION> with your values.

placeholders.name: OUTPUT_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the monitor output, e.g., HDMI-1

steps.explain: Optionally, set a specific refresh rate if multiple are available for the chosen resolution.

placeholders.name: OUTPUT_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the monitor output

placeholders.name: RATE
placeholders.description: The refresh rate in Hz, e.g., 60

alternatives.explain: Turn on the output and set the preferred (maximum) resolution automatically.

placeholders.name: OUTPUT_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the monitor output
